title_en: What Time Does It Open in Chinese

sentences.en: Sunday morning, I went to the bank, but the bank's door was closed, and there wasn't a single person around.
I asked the person next to me: "What time does the bank open?"
He said: "The bank opens at nine — it's only eight now."
I still had an hour to wait, so I went to look around a nearby shop first.
After a while, I went back to the bank and saw the door was open — inside, there were already many people.
I went in and waited too, and after half an hour, my business was done.
When I walked out of the bank, I checked the time — only ten o'clock — and I decided to go eat first.

quiz.q: What does the narrator find when arriving at the bank?
What time does the bank actually open?
What does the narrator do right after finishing at the bank?

grammar.p: 几点开门？(What time does it open?)
grammar.e: 几点 asks for a specific clock time; paired with 开门 (to open for business) or 关门 (to close), it's the standard way to ask a shop's hours.
grammar.x: 银行几点开门？— What time does the bank open?

grammar.p: 才 + time（only; not yet — something is earlier than expected）
grammar.e: 才 before a time expression shows that a point is still early, or hasn't been reached yet.
grammar.x: 银行九点开门，现在才八点。— The bank opens at nine, and it's only eight now.

grammar.e: 着 attached to a verb shows a state continuing — here, the door staying shut, and later, staying open.
grammar.x: 银行的门关着，一个人也没有。— The bank's door was closed, and there wasn't a single person around.
